name: shrink-compensated-cavity
source: mcweed U64 mold jig rev 1 ('the mold negatives now have a little bottom on them... we need some kind of lip there so that it creates a better seal') and U278 ('caliper 88.0mm vs CAD 87.16' -> the silicone/plaster oversize became a process rule), plus U225 demould draft ('taper those cavities so green ceramic teeth release').
summary: Build the mould cavity that casts a given puck, compensated for a 4% linear firing shrink. Four things compound: the factor is 1/0.96 = 1.041667 and not 1.04; the growth is about the part's own axis BEFORE placing, not about the world origin after; the growth is uniform so the 1 mm rim chamfer grows too; and the cavity is the part's negative, so the puck's blind bore comes out as a post of block material whose radius and height are scaled as well, standing on the cavity floor because the puck lies mouth-down. The asfailed reproduces 1.04 flat plus an unscaled chamfer. Both of those errors are a few hundredths of a millimetre, well under a grid cell: IoU and max_dev cannot see them and score ~1.000 / ~0. The probes that discriminate are cavity-wall-radius-is-compensated-not-4-percent (a 0.0167 mm band at r = 10.408), chamfer-face-sits-at-the-grown-position (a 0.0117 mm band; chamfer-width-grew-with-the-part is the coarser 0.042 mm version of the same check) and cavity-floor-is-at-the-grown-depth (a 0.0133 mm band). The coarser errors - no compensation at all, growth after placement, mouth-up orientation, missing chamfer - are caught by the guard probes and by max_dev.
